- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.28) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for downward bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above true) — cap forecast at 10% above recent peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or mildly negative), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true prices.
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms when sentiment is weak or mixed — apply a 1–3% upward bias to offset underestimation.
- If sentiment turns sharply bullish after a downtrend, model often fails to capture momentum — add 3–5% extra to forecast if sentiment >0.17 for 3+ consecutive days.
